proposal: Precompute the second server-receipt-elapsed authoritative replay before taking account/room locks, then use it only after the existing locked authority checks prove its inputs exactly equal the room contract.
judgment: Legitimate pure-computation relocation. It can shorten the serialized critical section without trusting client metrics or changing shared-clock acceptance, provided every condition below is retained.
requiredConditions: The receipt remains the DB clock sampled before either replay; it must never come from body fields or be refreshed after processing.

The client-elapsed SessionValidator.validate replay remains distinct from the second replay. The second replay uses min(duration,max(0,receipt-start)), server target semantics, no Arena pauses/segments and finiteFinal equal to finish.
A request-local private prepared context is created by ArenaEvidence.prepare, not read from the HTTP body. It retains the exact canonical validated candidate used for computation.

At the locked boundary recompute elapsed from the fetched room start and duration, and run validateIssued, shared-start binding, event-time bounds, immutable prefix, membership/terminal/stale/grace and finish checks as before.

Reuse requires exact equality of DB receipt, canonical candidate, actual shared start, duration, expected target, finish/finite flag and recomputed authoritative elapsed. Normalize numeric representation when creating context to match the existing DB-start float and room-duration integer.

A COW copy of the canonical candidate plus strict array equality binds configuration/events and all canonical evidence without rehashing that evidence inside the lock. Explicit named fields make the room binding auditable.

Absent, malformed or mismatched context executes the existing authoritative locked replay, not the candidate-elapsed validation result. Old direct two-argument prepare callers remain supported through that fallback.

No projection is accepted before the locked checks. Exact finished retries still return idempotently before stale checking/writes. Final settlement and serialization continue to sample current DB time.

The projection is never shared across requests/accounts/rooms and is not a reusable global cache. Existing CSRF/authentication, owner checks, quota, atomic writes and result overrides remain unchanged.
necessaryTests: At client elapsed1000 and DB receipt2000, cached and fallback paths produce the same authoritative18WPM and complete2000ms time series, differing from the36WPM client-elapsed validation projection.
Compare complete cached-versus-fallback member writes and replay outputs at ordinary, fractional, exactly capped deadline and finite-final partial-text boundaries.

Mismatch or remove each context binding: receipt, start, duration, target, finish, computed elapsed and canonical candidate/config/events. Require the old locked rejection or independent fallback, never an incompatible cached score.
Body-supplied authoritative/projection/receipt fields do not enter the trusted context.

Retain changed issued rules, start mismatch, changed stored prefix/session, forfeit, quarantine, completed room, stale elapsed, newer heartbeat, future-at-receipt evidence, grace expiry and unchanged finished retry cases.
Simulate receipt within grace but processing past grace: acceptance uses receipt, then final current-time settlement completes the room without reopening terminal state.
Retain canonical JS/PHP and stable-payload parity. Run native SQL/HTTP capacity after implementation; do not infer capacity improvement from pure protocol tests.
performanceLimit: This removes replay CPU from lock hold time but does not remove that CPU from each request. It may reduce contention; a submit p95 below150ms is unproven until the unchanged native capacity experiment runs.
